react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-direct activity) unanimously identify tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway in this treatment-vs-control comparison. RaMP ranked KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' at the top of 15 returned pathways with an FDR of 1.50e-14 and fold enrichment of 667, hitting six input metabolites (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, quinolinic acid, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed this same pathway (KEGG:hsa00380) as its sole genome-wide significant hit (p = 1.03e-06), matching five of the same compounds. The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm independently recovered 'Tryptophan metabolism' at its top rank (p = 0.0027) using the empirical human_mfn network, achieving near-complete pathway coverage (12 of 13 metabolite nodes present). The RaMP Reactome result 'Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis' (R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.47e-08) and the WikiPathways result 'Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production' (WP:WP4210, FDR 1.10e-10) further corroborate a coordinated perturbation spanning the serotonergic branch, the kynurenine/quinolinate branch, and the NAD+ biosynthetic branch of this amino-acid catabolic network. Five input metabolites are confirmed members of this metabolic network: L-tryptophan (the substrate entry point), serotonin and melatonin (neuroactive downstream products), and quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (kynurenine-pathway intermediates). Tryptamine, putrescine, L-leucine, and 3-sulfinoalanine were detected at lower signal intensity and likely reflect peripheral secondary effects. The convergent multi-paradigm signal across ORA, PSEA, and network-diffusion methods strongly indicates that experimental treatment reshapes central tryptophan catabolism, with implications for neuroactive signalling, immune regulation via the kynurenine axis, and NAD+-dependent energetics.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Multi-paradigm enrichment analysis of nine differentially abundant metabolites identified convergent perturbation of tryptophan metabolic networks. RaMP-DB ORA placed KEGG:map00380 "Tryptophan metabolism" as the top hit (FDR 1.50e-14), with six input metabolites confirmed as pathway members: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, quinolinic acid, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. WikiPathways WP:WP465 (FDR 1.26e-11) and WP:WP4210 "Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production" (FDR 1.10e-10) corroborated this signal across independent pathway databases. The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm on the human_mfn empirical network independently recovered the same KEGG "Tryptophan metabolism" module as its top-ranked hit (p = 0.00168) with eight of the input metabolites mapped to the network, confirming that metabolite identity—not mass alone—drives the enrichment. Driver-metabolite analysis identifies L-tryptophan as the entry substrate and serotonin and melatonin as neuroactive downstream products confirmed by REACT:R-HSA-209931 "Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis" (FDR 3.47e-08). Quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid route through the kynurenine arm of the pathway, linking tryptophan catabolism to NAD+ biosynthesis. Putrescine, L-leucine, and 3-sulfinoalanine appear in broader amino-acid metabolism networks (fold enrichment 667) and likely reflect secondary amino-group handling. The convergent signal across ORA and network-diffusion methods indicates the treatment robustly reshapes tryptophan catabolism with implications for neuroactive signalling and NAD+-dependent energetics.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-direct activity) unanimously identify tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway in this treatment-vs-control comparison. RaMP ranked KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' at the top of 15 returned pathways with an FDR of 1.50e-14 and fold enrichment of 667, hitting six input metabolites (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, quinolinic acid, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed this same pathway (KEGG:hsa00380) as its sole genome-wide significant hit (p = 1.03e-06), matching five of the same compounds. The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm independently recovered 'Tryptophan metabolism' at its top rank (p = 0.0027) using the empirical human_mfn network, achieving near-complete pathway coverage (12 of 13 metabolite nodes present). The RaMP Reactome result 'Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis' (R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.47e-08) and the WikiPathways result 'Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production' (WP:WP4210, FDR 1.10e-10) further corroborate a coordinated perturbation spanning the serotonergic branch, the kynurenine/quinolinate branch, and the NAD+ biosynthetic branch of this amino-acid catabolic network. Five input metabolites are confirmed members of this metabolic network: L-tryptophan (the substrate entry point), serotonin and melatonin (neuroactive downstream products), and quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (kynurenine-pathway intermediates). Tryptamine, putrescine, L-leucine, and 3-sulfinoalanine were detected at lower signal intensity and likely reflect peripheral secondary effects. The convergent multi-paradigm signal across ORA, PSEA, and network-diffusion methods strongly indicates that experimental treatment reshapes central tryptophan catabolism, with implications for neuroactive signalling, immune regulation via the kynurenine axis, and NAD+-dependent energetics.

RaMP ranked KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' at the top of 15 returned pathways with an FDR of 1.50e-14 and fold enrichment of 667, hitting six input metabolites (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, quinolinic acid, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed this same pathway (KEGG:hsa00380) as its sole genome-wide significant hit (p = 1.03e-06), matching five of the same compounds. The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm independently recovered 'Tryptophan metabolism' at its top rank (p = 0.0027) using the empirical human_mfn network, achieving near-complete pathway coverage (12 of 13 metabolite nodes present). The RaMP Reactome result 'Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis' (R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.47e-08) and the WikiPathways result 'Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production' (WP:WP4210, FDR 1.10e-10) further corroborate a coordinated perturbation spanning the serotonergic branch, the kynurenine/quinolinate branch, and the NAD+ biosynthetic branch of this amino-acid catabolic network. Five input metabolites are confirmed members of this metabolic network: L-tryptophan (the substrate entry point), serotonin and melatonin (neuroactive downstream products), and quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (kynurenine-pathway intermediates). Tryptamine, putrescine, L-leucine, and 3-sulfinoalanine were detected at lower signal intensity and likely reflect peripheral secondary effects.
